english: Let $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $G:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable functions such that $F'(x)=e^{5x}\sin12x$ and $G'(x)=F(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}F(x)=\lim_{x\to-\infty}G(x)=0$. Let $M$ be the maximum value of $e^{-5x}G(x)$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $\dfrac{1}{M}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ तथा $G:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ अवकलनीय फलन हैं जिनके लिए सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $F'(x)=e^{5x}\sin12x$ तथा $G'(x)=F(x)$ हैं, और $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}F(x)=\lim_{x\to-\infty}G(x)=0$ है। माना कि $\mathbb{R}$ पर $e^{-5x}G(x)$ का अधिकतम मान $M$ है। तब $\dfrac{1}{M}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $e^{5x}\to0$ as $x\to-\infty$, so the limit condition gives $C_{1}=0$
solution_full: Let $I=\displaystyle\int e^{5x}\sin12x\,dx$ and $J=\displaystyle\int e^{5x}\cos12x\,dx$. Integrating by parts with $e^{5x}$ as the function to integrate:
So $F(x)=\dfrac{e^{5x}(5\sin12x-12\cos12x)}{169}+C_{1}$. The bracket is bounded and $e^{5x}\to0$ as $x\to-\infty$, so $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}F=C_{1}=0$.
Hence $G(x)=\dfrac{e^{5x}(-119\sin12x-120\cos12x)}{28561}+C_{2}$, and the same limit argument gives $C_{2}=0$.
originality_note: New: the repeating-integral formula is applied twice (a second antiderivative), both constants are fixed by decay at minus infinity, and the amplitude of the second antiderivative turns out to be 1/169 through the triple 119-120-169 (way 1). Closest known: the single integral of e^(ax) sin(bx). Different because: the second antiderivative and its amplitude are asked, so the solver must iterate the formula and combine the sine and cosine integrals.
key_step: Applying the e^(ax) sin(bx) formula twice and computing the amplitude sqrt(119^2 + 120^2) = 169.
justification: A routine but multi-step chain of standard results (repeating integral twice, limit fixing constants, amplitude). No insight needed; numerical format but clean numbers. Level 2 like 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

concept_use.Repeating-integral technique: int e^(ax): The integrals of e^(5x) sin 12x and e^(5x) cos 12x are found by the repeating-integral method, solving for the integral that reappears.
concept_use.Integration by parts: Integration by parts, applied twice to each integral, produces the two linear equations in I and J that the repeating method solves.
